How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Catered accommodation included gym membership at David Ross Center. They offered en-suites rooms and rooms where you shared the toilet with 1 other person and rooms where you shared the toilet with up to 5 other people.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: they offered halal, vegetarian, kosher from what I am aware so they were very accommodating

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: most students who live on campus accommodation are first year students so 18-20 years olds on average.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: From what I remember there is one day sometime in the first week, where all the international and exchange student gather outside of Trent building to register WITH their passport and proof of flight ticket.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: every kind, the staff was very accommodating.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all 3 classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Honestly go for international law classes offered they are objectively so much easier, because it's something entirely different to study regional law.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 3 courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
it depends on the module, but they offered tutoring, which was a more intimate class with maybe 8-10 students where they exclusively covered exam content. 
classes are only 1 hour long. 
all their lectures are recorded and that was really helpful during the exam period.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Issues in Company Law 
International Humanitarian Law 
Foundations of Public International Law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
the international law courses, and if possible the ones with an assignment as the final exam. I knew an exchange student who was done with all exams in early January. 

if you do choose to take Issues in Company Law, Colin is genuinely one of the best teachers I have ever had.

Additional comments:
questions.answer:
They have a club for everything:
https://su.nottingham.ac.uk/activities/list

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: genuinely every kind, and you didn't even have to be from that ethnicity or whatever to join their events. Everyone was very open.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I quite enjoyed going to the gym at David Ross, I met some very nice people there. 
go hiking if can, we don't have that back home in Denmark.
go on day or weekend trips to neighboring cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
again, travel to neighboring cities.
go to a ice hockey game. 
attend a variety game between UoN and Trent.
picnic in the Downs with all your friends is a must. 
try all the different food places, Nottingham has Pepes, Wingstop, Nando's and so much more in city center. 
try boating on Highfields Lake. 
nottingham host events in city center like the Christmas market

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Nottingham has a very diverse community.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Talk to anyone and everyone. I cannot stress this enough everyone is so welcoming and everyone wants to make friends. 
have breakfast and dinner with new people as often as you can. 
speak to people in your halls.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the diversity and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
enjoy it, because time on exchange flies by. 
take photos and videos of everything anf everyone. 
say yes to plans, the most spontaneous plans ended up being the most memorable and enjoyable.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
George Green > Hallward library 
Portland is a great place to meet new people

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: you meet a different version of yourself on exchange, these new experiences, the exposure, it all shape you into something new.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I stayed over Christmas and when you become so accustomed to people around you at every hour of everyday. it was very hard to stay in a place that felt like a ghost town when everyone left for break. Because being on campus means mostly only student or faculty member are browsing around on the grounds. when everyone is gone, it is SO lonely.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
